title: Completion at a quasi-finite prime is a direct factor of the completed base change
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map where $R$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, and assume that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite] (affine case, Stacks Algebra Definition 00PL). Let $R_{\mathfrak p}$, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nR_{\mathfrak p}$, $(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^nS_{\mathfrak q}$ their completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\phi:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ be the natural ring map $x\otimes y\mapsto\hat\varphi(x)\cdot\iota(y)$, where $\hat\varphi:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is induced by the local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\iota:S\to S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is the canonical map. Then there are a ring $B$ and a ring map $\beta:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\to B$ such that $(\phi,\beta):(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\times B$ is a ring isomorphism. In particular $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\cong(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\times B$ as $S$-algebras and as $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebras, with $B$ an $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebra via $\beta$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime) and its proof, including the final 'sanity check' that the projection to $S_{\mathfrak q}^\wedge$ is the natural map (uses Lemma Tag 00QB lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure and Lemma Tag 07N9 lemma-completion-finite-extension); cited in More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PP
